chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn Maysarah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who sells his slave for less than his price so that he may be freed, and the slave says to him privately, “I owe you such-and-such.” Is it permissible for him to take it from him? He said:
He may take it from him voluntarily, and ask him for it gently; but if he refuses, then he should leave him.

key_terms.بِنُقْصَانٍ: at a reduction, for less than full value
key_terms.لِيُعْتَقَ: so that he may be freed

ai.seo_question: Can a person who sold a slave cheaply for emancipation later accept a promised payment from him?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a case involving the sale of a slave at a reduced price with the hope of emancipation, followed by a private promise of repayment from the slave. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام permits taking that amount only in a voluntary and gentle manner, without compulsion. If the former slave refuses, the seller is instructed to forgo the claim.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3562 - Muawiyah ibn Maytharah narrated from Abu Abdullah (as):

I asked him about a man who sells his slave at a reduced price so that he may be freed, and the slave says to him in private, "I will give you such-and-such amount."
Is it permissible for the man to take it from him?
Imam (as) replied: "He may take it from him willingly and ask him for it politely. But if the slave refuses, then let him leave it."
